# A common projective field on an aligned homothetic stratum

This is a positive interface for the new weighted conditional surface
transport theorem. On one genuinely homothetic aligned stratum, the
source projective fields can be normalized to coincide exactly, so their
actual maximum incurs no extra mismatch. The result does not glue distinct
strata or pay the total cost of contacts outside this stratum.

## 1. Hypotheses

Let C be the canonical convex hull of finitely many positive convex fibers
in R^n x R^d, d>=1. Let ell be a positive affine function on the entire base
polytope Q. Suppose a nonempty convex set F subset Q carries an affine
marked graph y:F->R^d and one convex body D containing0 in its interior,
with the ACTUAL fibers

    C_z=y(z)+ell(z)D,      z in F.                    (1)

This is exactly the marked-homothety conclusion already proved for one
aligned deepest stratum in
`candidate 3101206ec4580190`,
Section3. We do not infer (1) for unrelated deepest strata.

Let a_* be the unique projective normalizer of (D,0), and let E_*=E_D(0)>0.
For each source p in F, y(p) is its marked point. Its own projective
normalizer is a_p=a_*/ell(p), because its projective-volume objective is
ell(p)^d times that of D after this substitution.

## 2. One affine positive extension for every source in the stratum

There exists one affine function L on the full ambient space, positive
on all C, such that

    L(z,x)=ell(z)+a_* dot [x-y(z)]    for z in F.      (2)

More precisely, L>=min_Q ell/(d+1)>0 on C.

Here are the details ensuring this is a common extension. Put
G(z,x)=E_(C_z)(x)^(1/d). This function is jointly concave by the proved
energy theorem. Choose p in relint F and take a finite affine global
supergradient S of G at (p,y(p)), then divide S by E_*^(1/d). Existence,
including a projection-boundary p, is proved for canonical finite hulls
in `candidate c0fc791108fc8765`.
That theorem applies also when p was not originally sampled: add its
actual full-dimensional fiber as another finite sample; the canonical
hull is unchanged and the theorem only requires real, not integer, bases.

The resulting affine function S satisfies

    S(z,x)>=G(z,x)/E_*^(1/d)>0

at every interior-fiber point of C. Its continuous coefficient is
((d+1)/d)a_*: indeed G(p,y(p))=ell(p)E_*^(1/d) and the envelope derivative
is ((d+1)/d)G(p,y(p))a_p.

On the marked graph over F, both G/E_*^(1/d) and ell equal ell(z).
Hence the affine nonnegative function

    z -> S(z,y(z))-ell(z)

vanishes at p in relint F and must vanish identically on F. It follows
that, on every fiber above F,

    S(z,x)=ell(z)+((d+1)/d)a_* dot [x-y(z)].

Set

    L=(d/(d+1))S+(1/(d+1))ell.                       (3)

Then (2) holds. Positivity of S on the interior fibers and approximation
within each full-dimensional fiber give S>=0 on C. Equation(3) gives the
claimed common uniform positivity floor.

## 3. Common supporting planes and exact equality of the source fields

For each continuous normal u, the real fiber support h_z(u) is concave in
z. On F it is the affine function

    h_z(u)=u dot y(z)+ell(z)h_D(u).                  (4)

Choose a finite global affine support majorant A_u(z) touching at the same
p in relint F. The finite supporting-slope construction in
`candidate 6748c967393345b9` provides
such a majorant. As in Section2, its nonnegative affine difference from
(4) vanishes at a relative interior point, hence

    A_u(z)=h_z(u) for every z in F.                  (5)

One can use a continuous bounded choice in u from that construction.
Thus all sources in F may use this SAME global support plane.

At source p_i in F, let ell_i=ell(p_i). Its own support height is
H_i(u)=ell_i h_D(u), and the common denominator L/ell_i restricts on the
source fiber to its exact normalizing denominator
1+a_i dot(x-y(p_i)). It is therefore an admissible affine base extension
of the source chart.

The corresponding source potential, multiplied by the positive scalar
ell_i^(-(d+1)), is

    ell_i^(-(d+1)) H_i(u) [L(z,x)/ell_i]^(-d)
       =h_D(u)/L(z,x)^d.                            (6)

This equality holds throughout C, not just at the source. Since every
source uses (5), their scaled global supporting cuts are exactly the same
cuts, including the contact set. Applying finitely many of them takes the
maximum of IDENTICAL boundary fields; it does not increase the speed.
If a globally finite convex continuation is needed outside C, use one
tangent continuation of t^-d below the common positivity floor for L;
rescaling its threshold by ell_i gives equality in (6) globally as well.

The actual speed from these common cuts is therefore

    v_z(x)=h_D(n_z(x))/L(z,x)^d

at the contact boundary points of A_u and zero at the other points. This
is exactly one common inverse-power field, rather than a maximum of
different source denominators. Its conditional weights have the new
weighted density-selection form with constant positive H=h_D(u) at each
fixed normal. The conditional surface density g is the actual one supplied
by the normal-disintegration theorem; it is not replaced by uniform face
measure when that conditional law is nonuniform.

## 4. Exact source costs, and what is not yet paid

The own-fiber total cost of the common field at p_i is

    D_i^common=d E_*/ell_i.                           (7)

Indeed the original source projective image has volume ell_i^d E_*, so
its original projective boundary cost is d ell_i^d E_*; multiply by the
scalar ell_i^(-(d+1)) from (6). Every ambient halfspace containing the
marked point (p_i,y(p_i)) receives at least Gamma_d times (7) from that
source fiber, by the ordinary projective-centroid boundary theorem.

Formula(7) is inverse in ell_i, not proportional to the actual volume
ell_i^d|D|. It must not be silently substituted for mixed volume in a
budget calculation. Other fibers may share the same global support
planes and incur additional costs under (6), even when they do not lie
in the homothetic stratum. This note gives no upper bound for that extra
cost and no all-row critical cap-payment theorem.

The useful new conclusion is exact compatibility WITHIN each already
proved aligned homothetic stratum. The maximum-field counterexamples in
`candidate 513a098b26545097`
use distinct unaligned charts and do not contradict (6). To continue
this route one must either coordinate different strata or prove that
outside contact costs can be charged through the selected critical
structure; the weighted transport theorem alone does not do this.

## 5. The common contact mask is preserved by midpoint repair

There is no additional capacity loss from restricting this common field to
its actual support-contact mask. Fix u and its affine support majorant
A_u(z). If two physical endpoint support points satisfy

    u dot x_i=h_(z_i)(u)=A_u(z_i),

their midpoint satisfies u dot x_mid=A_u(z_mid) by affinity. Convex-body
containment places this midpoint in C_(z_mid), while the global support
majorant gives u dot x_mid<=h_(z_mid)(u)<=A_u(z_mid). Both inequalities
are therefore equalities. The midpoint is on the actual target support
face and its base remains in the common contact set.

Thus every product coupling of endpoint marginals on this one common
mask stays on that mask at its midpoint whenever its averaged base is
integer. The weighted parity replacement may be applied within it with
exactly the same target field. This closes a potential masking issue,
not the numerical cost of other stratum-exterior fibers belonging to the
same mask. This observation was independently checked by research-agent.
